KNOWN LIMITS OF THE TASK THIS WAS MADE ON, SAID PLAINLY: the cost of a motor-out flight charges the sink at first contact, the speed over the ground there (0.4 for each 5 m/s, up to 2.0: a stand-in that was CHOSEN and not measured for a roll-over limit the model does not have), whether the machine is still standing four seconds later, and a crash by the speed it hit at (3 + 4 x speed / 25); so a pilot is not rewarded for carrying speed in, but nothing makes a fast landing tip over and what a real machine would walk away from is not claimed. The world is the task's own -- flat ground, no obstacle, a wind of two sinusoids a side, a motor that stops dead and whole, a full battery -- and none of it is a measurement of a real quadrotor (see the gate: tools/ship/trainDronePilot-selfcheck.mjs). AND THE MOTOR-OUT CORNER IS NOT SOLVED, WHICH IS WHAT THE TRAINING WAS FOR: the hand pilot lands none of the motor-out flights (every one ends crashed at 14 to 42 m/s) and a trained pilot may land none either, so a better motor-out score can be only a SLOWER CRASH (3 + 4 x speed / 25) -- the file's `by` quotes how many flights end not standing so that it can be seen.
